passage:
On the colony ground, Naveen and Vandana were the captains for the cricket match. Naveen chose first. “Aryan!” Aryan, the best batter, jumped up grinning. Vandana chose next. “Meera, she's our fastest fielder.” They went back and forth, and Naveen felt tall and proud, like a king. The circle shrank. Only Tanay was left, hands in pockets, looking at his shoes.

Naveen noticed. He remembered the day Tanay had caught three balls at the fence. “Tanay, you're my wicketkeeper,” he said. Tanay's shoulders lifted. Vandana muttered, “We didn't have a keeper anyway.” Naveen grinned. “Now we do.”

qa.q: Who did Naveen pick first?
qa.a: Naveen picked Aryan first.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling when choosing first?
qa.a: Naveen felt tall and proud, like a king, at having the first pick.

qa.q: What choice did Naveen make about Tanay, and why?
qa.a: Naveen remembered Tanay's three catches at the fence and chose Tanay as wicketkeeper, giving the team a strength it lacked.

qa.q: How might Tanay have felt standing with hands in pockets and then hearing a name called?
qa.a: Tanay probably felt anxious and small while waiting, then relieved and proud to be picked for a real role.

grounding: A child choosing sides feels the pride of first pick, and learns that a team needs different strengths.

passage:
“Rock, paper, scissors for first pick,” Swati said. “I won. Meher.”

“Fine. Zoya,” said Jahnavi.

“Aditya.”

“Priya. She's fast.”

Swati grinned. “Ooh, we'll beat you.” Then she glanced around. Only three children were left: Kabir, Ritu and little Sunil, who studied the ground.

“You go,” Jahnavi whispered. “We can't pick only the fast ones.”

“Kabir's slow.”

“He keeps score best. Ritu remembers all the rules. And Sunil throws well when nobody's watching.”

Swati paused. “Okay. Kabir, you keep score. Ritu, you hold the whistle. Sunil, you throw first.”

Sunil looked up quickly. “Really?”

“Really,” said Swati, and meant it.

qa.q: How did the captains decide who picks first?
qa.a: They played rock, paper, scissors, and Swati won.

qa.q: Why did Sunil look up quickly and ask, “Really?”
qa.a: Sunil was surprised and hopeful, having expected to be picked last and hardly believing being given a real job.

qa.q: What did Swati change after Jahnavi whispered about the remaining children?
qa.a: Swati stopped choosing only the fastest and gave Kabir, Ritu and Sunil roles that used their strengths.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi see what a team needs?
qa.a: Jahnavi sees that a team needs different strengths, like scorekeeping, rule-keeping and throwing, not just speed.

grounding: Children choosing sides feel the pride of being picked first, and learn that a team needs different strengths.

passage:
The rain was coming, so the match had to be only six overs. Hrithik was captain and had one minute to pick the team.
Everyone wanted the fast runners. Vaibhav stood at the end, looking at his shoes. He was the slowest boy in the class, and he knew it. Last time he'd been picked last.
Hrithik picked two fast bowlers first, feeling proud as they cheered. Then he remembered: in the rain, the ball would be slippery, and Vaibhav was the best wicketkeeper in their colony.
“Vaibhav,” he called, third.
Vaibhav looked up, surprised.
He took two catches in the rain. After the match, the fast bowlers carried him on their shoulders. Hrithik thought: a team needs different people.

qa.q: How many overs was the match?
qa.a: Only six overs.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel when Hrithik called his name?
qa.a: He felt surprised and happy, after expecting to be picked last again.

qa.q: What did Hrithik learn about choosing a team?
qa.a: That a team needs different strengths, like Vaibhav's safe hands in the rain, not just fast runners.

qa.q: How might the fast bowlers have felt after the match?
qa.a: They seemed happy and grateful, carrying Vaibhav on their shoulders after his catches.

grounding: Shows a child captain, picking teams under time pressure, noticing that a team needs different strengths beyond speed.

passage:
At the colony cricket game in Pune, Chinmay was always picked first. He loved the moment when captains shouted his name, and the others looked at him with envy.
Naveen was always picked last. He shrugged and said, “Whatever.”
One Sunday, Chinmay's team was losing badly. Their fast bowlers were being hit everywhere. Naveen, who nobody had asked to bowl, said quietly, “Can I try? I bowl slow spin.”
He took three wickets in two overs.
On the way home, Chinmay walked next to Naveen. “Why didn't you ever say you bowl spin?”
Naveen shrugged. “Nobody picks the spinner first.”
Chinmay thought about that all evening.

qa.q: How many wickets did Naveen take?
qa.a: Three wickets in two overs.

qa.q: How did Chinmay feel when captains shouted his name?
qa.a: He felt proud and pleased, enjoying being picked first while others looked at him with envy.

qa.q: What could the captains do next time they choose teams?
qa.a: They could think about what the team needs, like a spinner, rather than just picking the fastest and most popular.

qa.q: How might Naveen feel about always being picked last?
qa.a: He probably feels hurt, though he shrugs and says "Whatever" to hide it.

grounding: Shows a child who enjoys being picked first learning that a team needs different strengths when the last-picked boy wins the game.

passage:
“Madhuri, you're captain, you pick first,” said the PE sir.
“Pankaj!” Madhuri called at once. He was the strongest raider in the kabaddi team.
“Rohit!”
“Sunny!” She was choosing all the big boys.
Pankaj leaned over. “Madhuri, who's going to defend? We need someone who holds.”
“Defending is boring.”
“Take Jyoti. She never lets go of an ankle.”
Madhuri looked at Jyoti, small and quiet. She hesitated. Then, “Jyoti!”
In the match, Jyoti held two raiders in a row. Madhuri's team won by three points.
“Okay,” Madhuri admitted, grinning. “Maybe teams need different people.”

qa.q: By how many points did Madhuri's team win?
qa.a: By three points.

qa.q: How did Madhuri feel when Pankaj suggested Jyoti?
qa.a: She felt unsure and hesitant, since Jyoti was small and quiet, before deciding to trust the suggestion.

qa.q: What went well once Madhuri took Pankaj's advice?
qa.a: Picking a defender as well as raiders gave the team different strengths, and Jyoti's holding helped them win.

qa.q: How might Jyoti have felt being picked by the captain?
qa.a: She was probably surprised and proud, getting a chance to show her skill.

grounding: Shows a child captain picking teams, feeling the pull of choosing the strongest, and learning that a team needs different strengths.

passage:
I'm Irfan. Last Friday in games period, Sir made me and Rohan captains for football. I felt like a king.
I picked the fast boys first: Sameer, then Kunal, then Ali. Soon only Yogesh was left. He's slow and wears thick glasses. I sighed loudly and said, "Fine, Yogesh." His face went red.
In the match, the other team kept scoring from long kicks. Then Yogesh said, "Put me in goal. I'm good at watching." I didn't believe him, but I let him. He saved three shots! We won 3–2.
On the way back, I told him sorry for the sigh. Next time I'll think about what each person is good at, not just who runs fastest.

qa.q: How many shots did Yogesh save?
qa.a: He saved three shots.

qa.q: Why did Irfan say sorry on the way back?
qa.a: Irfan felt guilty and a bit ashamed of the loud sigh after seeing how much Yogesh helped the team win.

qa.q: What will Irfan do differently when picking a team next time?
qa.a: Think about what each person is good at, like watching the ball in goal, not only speed.

qa.q: What was it like for Yogesh to be picked last with a sigh?
qa.a: Yogesh felt embarrassed and hurt, his face going red, before getting a chance to show his strength.

grounding: Shows children choosing sides, with the pride of picking first and the sting of being picked last, and learning a team needs different strengths.
